pr_title: RFC: hassio: Retry supervisor API when not ready (work-around race-condition between supervisor and core)
pr_body:
## Proposed change
This is an RFC for a change to address a race condition between supervisor and core especially on fast machines. As described in #95887 after rebooting HAOS / HA supervised core and supervisor may be coming up in parallel and supervisor API may not be ready in time to reply to core API requests ` HassioAPIError('System is not ready with state: setup')` and this situation is not dealt with in core adequately, occasionally causing the first startup of core after a reboot to fail and requiring a manual restart of core.

I have first tried to address this on supervisor side, but my PR was closed without useful feedback as to how to address the situation instead: https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/pull/4428

I'm well aware that the proposed change is probably not clean so more or less looking for feedback and trying to get the attention of someone with more insight.

issue_context.title: First HA core start after reboot fails (possible race condition with HA supervisor startup)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Every so often after a HAOS reboot the first start of HA core fails and HA core needs to be restarted manually for it to come up fully. The error logs indicate that at the time of failure HA core cannot communicate with HA supervisor API and a proper retry logic seems to be missing. This causes also some integrations to break at startup, e.g. ssdp. Supervisor logs shows no errors or warnings.

So all 3 of these logs are actually coming from error suppression. 

`Can't read panel info` comes from here when an error is prevented from bubbling:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/78222bd51cda9177a6dfa664933fa1bd25d7bda5/homeassistant/components/hassio/addon_panel.py#L78-L79

`Can't read Supervisor data` comes from here, also to prevent bubbling:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/78222bd51cda9177a6dfa664933fa1bd25d7bda5/homeassistant/components/hassio/__init__.py#L533-L534

`Failed to update supervisor issues` comes from here, again the error is suppressed:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/78222bd51cda9177a6dfa664933fa1bd25d7bda5/homeassistant/components/hassio/issues.py#L310-L312

In all 3 of these cases nothing actually breaks. That particular call to get current data from supervisor has failed. But all 3 of these occur in code called as part of a regular update loop that is polling supervisor. So next polling iteration setup has completed and the data is correctly pulled. This isn't to say these should be there. Log noise is bad since it causes people to spend time looking into it when really its meaningless. We do need to get rid of this but this isn't what is breaking the system.

However I note you said this:
> This causes also some integrations to break at startup, e.g. ssdp.

`ssdp` does in fact have a bug which is currently being worked on https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/96492 . `ssdp` currently depends on the `hassio` integration but doesn't list `hassio` as a dependency. This creates a race condition and if `ssdp` loads before `hassio` has finished loading it will crash.

The root cause of had nothing to do with the logs shown above. Rather it was because it used a helper that used the `hassio` integration under the hood, creating a dependency the developer was likely unaware of. You said `e.g. ssdp` implying that there were other broken integrations. Can you provide a list? If there are other integrations with a surprise dependency on `hassio` we need to address that.

> I guess for the long run there should be some sort of logic in HAOS/supervisor that HA core is delayed until supervisor and addons are up and functional (with some sort of docker health check or so).

@sbyx  Actually as of https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/pull/4376 Supervisor does wait until a healthcheck reports as healthy to decide if an addon is started. If an addon has a healthcheck anyway, most do not currently. Core does not currently have a healthcheck but supervisor has always had its own form of that by waiting until it can talk to core's API before considering it started:
https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/blob/98f2e3071c16c0373c2d5fc750c1b409ea4c9c41/supervisor/homeassistant/core.py#L314

The problem though is you're assuming core is supposed to be the last thing started. This is not true. A lot of addons must be started after core because they depend on core. VSCode, Node RED and AppDaemon for example are all extremely popular addons which talk to core and thus need it to be running first. Addon developers actually explicitly tell supervisor when to start their addon via the [`startup` config option](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/add-ons/configuration#optional-configuration-options):

> `initialize` will start the add-on on setup of Home Assistant. `system` is for things like databases and not dependent on other things. `services` will start before Home Assistant, while `application` is started afterwards. Finally `once` is for applications that don't run as a daemon.

Supervisor doesn't consider setup to be complete until it has started everything it needs to start. That includes core, the plugins and all addons which run as daemons in each of the 4 stages.

I'm not exactly sure what the solution is yet but starting core last isn't an option as it would break many addons.

@mdegat01 it is good that the infrastructure is there, however, it is curious that in the cases where I have seen the issue happening all docker containers were starting in parallel, even sometimes it seemed core before supervisor. So maybe there is something not working as expected.

And you are right of course there needs to be proper dependency tracking between containers not simply core being last.
